title: Lobbyist registry and municipal accommodation tax programs
subtitle: Also covered: Greener Homes loan changes, updated water and sewer by-laws, and staff and facility awards.
overview: The Committee of the Whole recommended that the City Clerk draft a lobbyist registry by-law and code of conduct, to return to Council in the third quarter of 2024 {{vote:m6}}. It also recommended approval of a Municipal Accommodation Tax administration policy and three funding programs for tourism and events, starting in the second quarter of 2024 {{vote:m7}}.

The committee recommended updates to the Guelph Greener Homes loan program by-law {{vote:m8}}. Through the consent report, it recommended approving the 2023 water services reports, a special charge by-law for Greener Homes, and updated Water and Sewer Use by-laws {{vote:m1}}. The committee also recognized staff and City facilities for awards.

For residents, the registry would make public who lobbies elected officials and senior staff, and when. The accommodation tax programs set out how hotel-stay revenue will support tourism projects and events. The Greener Homes change is meant to ease cash flow for households taking part. All of these recommendations go to Council for a final decision.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended directing the City Clerk to draft a Lobbyist Registry By-law and Code of Conduct and report back to Council in Q3 2024 {{vote:m6}}.

decisions.item: Municipal Accommodation Tax policy and funding programs
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the administration policy, the Destination Animation, Gather Here Sponsorship and Destination Gaps and Needs programs from Q2 2024, and delegating funding awards to the Deputy CAO of Public Services {{vote:m7}}.
The committee recommended authorizing updates to the Guelph Greener Homes Loan Program By-law {{vote:m8}}.
The committee recommended approving the special charge by-law and allowing future amendments to go directly on Council agendas without a staff report {{vote:m3}}.
The committee recommended approving an updated Sewer Use By-law that repeals and replaces the 1996 by-law {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended approving an updated Water By-law that repeals and replaces the 1991 by-law {{vote:m5}}.
The committee recommended approving the 2023 Water Services annual and summary reports and receiving the Water Efficiency Strategy progress report {{vote:m2}}.

debate: Several councillors asked whether non-profit and community groups should be covered by the lobbyist registry. Staff said the draft focuses on financial or business interest, and promised to address non-profits, with a recommendation, in the July report.

Councillors raised cases the registry might not cover. These included mass constituent emails, neighbours opposing a development, and groups opposing a project with no financial stake. Staff said these would generally fall outside the draft definition, but Council can define lobbying in the by-law.

One councillor asked for a public record of how members vote. Staff said that is outside this by-law and would need system changes. Others urged that the registry not discourage residents from contacting the City.

A delegate from a multisport event said it had received little City support and asked how such events could qualify for accommodation tax funding. Councillors asked staff how funding decisions would be made.

Councillors questioned the funding split. One said the city's share of Gather Here sponsorship funding seemed small given its link to hotel stays. Staff said the chamber would contribute larger amounts, that decisions would use a staff rubric, and that allocations could change.
